name: Yusuf Abbott

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m from the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to AI companies, employers, unions, political parties or government. We sell nothing and campaign for no side. This is confidential. What does a regular day at work look like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I’m 43 and supervise four people who manage lease renewals for a large company’s shops. I check rent changes, repair obligations and deadline letters before the property director signs. I only became a manager this year, and I still ask my longest-serving colleague to check the hard clauses. I like walking a shop with the owner and seeing why a repair matters; I dislike telling my team to hurry when I was the one who read a clause slowly.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What is home like, and how much financial room do you have?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My wife, Salma, works at a pharmacy, and our children are eleven and fifteen. I have a bachelor’s degree, high pay for a manager here and about eleven months of expenses saved; we still have a mortgage. There are plenty of similar offices nearby, although I know I’m a new manager rather than a star. I have never used an AI tool and prefer the signed lease and a call with the shop owner.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say the lease still needs a person to read the repair clause before it is signed. A bit of saved typing is fine, but I would not call it a change in the work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d be comfortable keeping this job while I learn it properly. Eleven months saved and Salma’s pharmacy wage mean we can handle an ordinary gap without moving the children.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I’d keep the Tuesday lease review with my experienced colleague and phone each shop owner before a disputed repair charge goes upstairs. In the first year Salma and I would keep paying an extra 180 monthly against the mortgage while both wages hold.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel calm. My main worry would still be getting a clause wrong, not losing the whole office.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why the extra mortgage payment now?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: We want the loan smaller before our older child leaves school. I would not send that 180 if Salma’s hours dropped.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you let a tool summarize the lease?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d let a colleague show me a sample, but I would read the signed pages myself. I have not used AI and do not want a summary to become the decision.

say: I’d keep a **person reading** each repair clause.
Saved typing would not change the **lease decision**.
I’d call the **shop owner** before approving a disputed repair.
think: I can keep learning this **manager job** while the lease office stays open.
Our **eleven-month reserve** and Salma’s pharmacy wage cover an ordinary income gap.
do: Keep **Tuesday lease reviews** and call owners about disputed repairs.
Pay **180 extra monthly** on the mortgage while both wages hold.
feel: I feel **calm** about work and household money.
S0.quote: I have not used AI and do not want a summary to become the decision.
fieldNote: He trusts **signed pages** and owner calls over summaries.
High pay and **eleven months saved** buffer an ordinary disruption.
Mortgage overpayments depend on **both wages** continuing.

steps.text: Keep Tuesday lease reviews and call owners about disputed repair charges
Pay an extra 180 monthly against the mortgage while both wages hold

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell my director that rent checking and deadline letters are exactly the tasks AI can take. I’d ask for a list of errors and a named person responsible before using it on live leases.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A tool might leave my colleague checking exceptions and remove the junior manager between her and the director. I have time to search because of the savings, but I doubt another lease office will be untouched.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This quarter I’d ask my colleague to compare twenty old lease summaries with signed pages and tell me where the software fails. In the first year I’d sit through a paid demonstration and use the tool myself only if it catches all repair obligations in those twenty; I’d quietly check posted roles at nearby firms rather than resign.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’m anxious about being the spare layer, though I can pay the mortgage during a search. I dislike depending on a tool I do not understand.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would make you trust the demonstration?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d want every repair obligation and notice date visible next to the signed line. A polished screen is not evidence that the shop owner will be paid.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why look at nearby firms if their desks may change too?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Some might need a manager for a few years, and I can ask what the actual vacancy is. I will not call a lateral move a permanent shelter from this.

say: I’d demand **lease-error counts** before live use.
A **named reviewer** should own repair and notice decisions.
I’d check every **notice date** against the signed line.
think: The junior manager could become a **spare layer**.
Other lease offices may face **similar cuts** despite my reserve.
do: Ask my **experienced colleague** to compare twenty old AI lease summaries with signed pages.
Use the tool only after a **paid demonstration** proves repair obligations are caught.
feel: I feel **anxious** about my place in the team.
S1.quote: A polished screen is not evidence that the shop owner will be paid.
fieldNote: He looks for **missing obligations** in signed leases.
He will try AI only after **successful paid evidence**.
Nearby offices offer vacancies but not **lasting safety** from the same tasks.

steps.text: Learn the lease tool only if a paid demonstration catches every repair obligation

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d ask the company for written closure dates and what happens to each lease account. Shop owners should not be sent to an unanswerable inbox when a repair invoice is disputed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My checking and negotiation notes are thinking work, so I expect my post to go in 2028. The physical shop visits might still need people until robots arrive around 2031, but I cannot pay a mortgage on a few visits alone.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This week Salma and I would put the older child’s planned private college deposit on hold and review public and apprenticeship options together. Before 2028 I’d ask three local property firms about paid site roles and request written severance terms; in the first year after AGI, I’d take a posted site job only if the written wage covers our mortgage and gives me real visits.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’m alarmed by losing a high wage, even with eleven months saved. I would not use our children’s education money to pretend I have a new career.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would you explain the deposit decision to your older child?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d show them the numbers and say an apprenticeship with a wage is an honest option, not a punishment. I would not choose their future without them.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if none of the site jobs pays enough?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d use the reserve for a measured search and keep the mortgage current. I would not buy a small business just to feel employed.

say: I’d seek **written closure dates** for lease accounts.
Shop owners need a **real repair contact** after desk changes.
think: Physical visits may last until **2031 robots**, but not replace my wage alone.
do: Pause the **private college deposit** while discussing options with Salma and our child.
Ask about **paid site vacancies** and accept only a written, mortgage-covering offer after 2028.
feel: I feel **alarmed** about losing a high wage.
S2.quote: I would not use our children’s education money to pretend I have a new career.
fieldNote: He makes a **family education decision** with Salma and their older child.
He expects his **2028 desk role** to go before 2031 robots.
A site move requires **written pay** and real visits, not a title.

steps.text: Pause the older child’s private college deposit while reviewing alternatives as a family
Ask three local property firms about paid site vacancies before 2028

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say five years gives families and companies time to sort out honest offers instead of talking about hope. I’d ask the firm to publish any real site posts before it cuts the lease desk.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I could keep earning while our older child finishes school, and then choose whether a site job actually suits me. The paperwork and judgment in that site job would still face AGI in 2031, while physical visits face robots around 2034.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Next year I’d arrange two paid site days with a local property firm only if my director agrees to release me, and I’d keep my lease manager job during that check. Before 2031 I’d apply for a posted site lease role only if it includes paid visits and covers our mortgage; after AGI arrives, I’d stay only while paid human inspections remain.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’m anxious, but five years means I can inspect an actual building before changing my pay. I would not jump into a role because it has a different name.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would a different office manager job solve the problem?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only for a while. An office manager job is still paperwork and judgment that AGI could take in 2031.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why insist on paid site days?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A company should pay for work it asks me to try. I have savings, but I will not use leave from my present job to fill another firm’s rota for free.

say: I’d ask for **real site posts** before desk cuts.
Families need **honest offers** during the five-year window.
A different desk job would still face **thinking AI**.
think: Physical visits face **2034 robots**, so a site title is limited shelter.
do: Arrange **two paid site days** only with director approval.
Apply for a **posted site role** only if visits and mortgage-covering pay are real.
Keep the **site role** after 2031 only while paid human inspections remain.
feel: I feel **anxious** but able to inspect the work.
S3.quote: An office manager job is still paperwork and judgment that AGI could take in 2031.
fieldNote: He uses **paid site days** to test the work without resigning.
He sees a site role’s **thinking tasks** exposed at AGI arrival.
The move requires **director approval** and mortgage-covering wages for real visits.

steps.text: Work two paid site days only if his director releases him

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say a decade gives employers time to explain the end of lease administration and give workers real choices. I’d want dates for notices and wage offers, not a glossy plan.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be 53 in 2036, with both children grown. If Salma and I keep earning, we can shrink the mortgage and keep an eleven-month reserve before my desk work changes. A property field title still has reports and decisions exposed to 2036 AGI, while robots reach visits around 2039.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In January 2027 I’d ask the lender for an extra-payment schedule and keep paying 180 monthly while both wages hold. I’d arrange one paid property site day each year with my director’s approval and apply for a posted field vacancy before 2036 only if it has real visits and a written wage covering the mortgage; in the first year after AGI, I’d remain only while paid human inspections exist.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy about leaving a job I know, but I can use ten years to make the mortgage smaller. I would rather have a paid choice than a new badge for the same exposed desk work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you use savings to buy a shop?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. Our reserve is for the family, and I would not borrow against the house to buy a job.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell your younger child?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say the family is keeping the mortgage small so they can choose their studies without panic. I would not promise that my title lasts forever.

A glossy plan is no substitute for **real choices**.
Workers need a **written offer** before leaving a lease desk.
think: I can reduce the **mortgage** before age 53 if Salma and I keep earning.
A field title still has **2036 thinking tasks** and 2039 robot exposure.
do: Keep paying **180 extra monthly** while both wages hold.
Take **paid yearly site days** and seek a written, mortgage-covering field offer.
Stay in the **field role** after 2036 only while paid human inspections exist.
feel: I feel **uneasy** but have time to reduce debt.
S4.quote: I would rather have a paid choice than a new badge for the same exposed desk work.
fieldNote: He prefers **mortgage reduction** to buying a speculative shop.
He expects **2036 AGI** to reach field paperwork before 2039 robots reach visits.
His site role requires **paid visits** and written wages.

steps.text: Pay an extra 180 monthly on the mortgage while both wages hold

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because my lease desk and high wage could disappear before our older child chooses a study route. Written severance, a posted site job with real pay and enough notice for our family to decide together would help. I do not want a handout or a risky purchase disguised as work.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn’t ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask who tells a shop owner that the repair clause still matters after the lease office closes. A signed lease does not repair a roof by itself.

headlineQuote: A signed lease does not repair a roof by itself.
portrait: **Yusuf**, 43, is a new lease-renewal manager with a bachelor’s degree.
High pay and **eleven months saved** protect a mortgage and two school-age children.
He has **never used AI** and requires successful signed-lease checks before learning it.
He chooses **mortgage reduction** and conditional paid site work over buying a business.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could end his lease desk while the family weighs an older child’s study costs.
whatWouldHelp: **Written severance**, a genuinely paid site vacancy and time for a family decision would help.
